sections.h2: Where is Campbell County, Wyoming, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Campbell County sits in northeast Wyoming, with Gillette as both the county seat and the largest city. Wikipedia lists the county at about 4,800 square miles, and it was created on February 21, 1911, from land taken from Crook and Weston Counties.

The neighbors are Powder River County, Montana, to the north, Crook and Weston Counties to the east, Converse County to the south, and Johnson and Sheridan Counties to the west. The county forms the Gillette micropolitan area. Gillette itself was founded in 1891 as a Burlington railroad town and was incorporated on January 6, 1892, according to its Wikipedia entry.

That is a very large county with very few people per square mile. For a seller, the practical result is that parcels range from small city lots in Gillette to rural acreage, and the same assessor and treasurer handle all of them.

sections.h2: What are the key numbers for Campbell County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts the Campbell County population at 48,145 as of July 1, 2025. The table below collects the figures we confirmed from the Census QuickFacts page and the county offices.

With nearly 78 percent of households owning their home, most Campbell County property tax bills land on families, not landlords.

sections.h2: How does coal shape the Campbell County tax base?
sections.html:
Coal makes up a large share of what Campbell County taxes. A WyoFile report from November 2021 said the county and Gillette supply about 40 percent of the nation's coal for electricity, and that coal was about 51.6 percent of the county's assessed value in 2021, down from 58.6 percent in 2017.

The same report said assessed valuation fell by $850 million from 2020 to 2021, the lowest level since 2004. Those are 2021 figures, so check the current numbers with the assessor.

Why does this matter to a homeowner? Wyoming taxes minerals and industrial property very differently from houses. The Wyoming Taxpayers Association guide lists minerals at 100 percent of fair market value, industrial property at 11.5 percent, and all other real and personal property at 9.5 percent. When the mine and industrial base changes, the mill levy spread across homes can change with it.

sections.h2: How is a Campbell County house assessed and taxed?
sections.html:
A Campbell County house is valued as of January 1, multiplied by 9.5 percent, then multiplied by the total mill levy for its location. The University of Wyoming Extension says residential levies run from 65 to 80 mills depending on location, with one mill equal to $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Here is how the math works on a hypothetical $279,100 house, the county median from the Census table above, at an illustrative 70 mills:

  • Assessed value: $279,100 x 9.5% = about $26,515
  • Tax before exemptions: $26,515 x 0.070 = about $1,856

That is an example, not your bill. Your actual mills depend on the city, school and special districts that cover your parcel.

The assessor and the treasurer do different jobs. The Assessor's Office values property and says it does not set tax amounts or collect taxes. The Treasurer bills and collects.

sections.h2: What exemptions and refunds can reduce a Campbell County bill?
sections.html:
Wyoming's 2025 law, Senate File 69, gives owner-occupied homes an exemption of 25 percent of the first $1 million of value. The legislative summary says it applies from tax year 2025 and, starting in tax year 2026, requires the owner to live in the home at least eight months a year.

A February 2026 Wyoming Public Media story reported that owners had to file an affidavit with the county assessor by March 1 that year. Ask the Campbell County assessor what the filing rule is for the next tax year.

  • The exemption covers an owner-occupied single-family house, condo, townhouse or manufactured home.
  • Someone who receives the long-term homeowner exemption on the same property cannot also take it for the same year.
  • The Campbell County Treasurer's page links to a Property Tax Refund Program.

A rental or a vacant inherited house does not meet the eight-month residence test, so check with the assessor before assuming the exemption applies.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Campbell County assessment?
sections.html:
You start by filing a written statement with the county assessor within 30 days after the assessment schedule was sent. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 sets that window, and the statement has to say why the assessment is wrong.

The Campbell County Assessor's page links to an Appeals Process page and an Important Dates page, so use those for this year's calendar. In Laramie County, for comparison, the county page says schedules are mailed on or before the fourth Monday of April and that owners can ask for an informal review before a formal appeal.

Gather what a board would want to see:

  • Your notice of value and parcel number
  • Recent sales of similar Gillette or rural houses, if you have them
  • Photos and repair estimates for condition problems the assessor may not have seen
  • An appraisal, if you ordered one

Residential sales data is confidential in Wyoming, so the office may not email or phone it to you.

sections.h2: What does Gillette's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Gillette gets about 17.59 inches of precipitation a year and about 55.7 inches of snow, according to the city's Wikipedia climate summary. May is the wettest month at 3.27 inches, and December through February each average 8 to 9 inches of snow.

Buyers and appraisers notice roofs, furnaces and foundations first in a climate like that. A house with an old roof or a failing heating system may be assessed on the same basis as its neighbors even though it needs money spent on it. If that describes your property, say so in writing when you ask for a review.

sections.h2: How does a Campbell County tax sale work?
sections.html:
In Campbell County the treasurer does not sell your house. The county sells its tax lien to a bidder, and the county's tax sale page describes the sale as buyer beware.

  • Notice of the sale and the list of properties is published three consecutive weeks in a legal newspaper in the county.
  • The buyer pays the unpaid taxes, interest and costs, and receives a certificate of purchase the day of the sale.
  • An owner can redeem by paying the tax sold, a 3% penalty, 15% simple interest, a redemption fee and any later taxes the holder paid.
  • Applying for a tax deed requires the holder to show compliance with Wyoming Statute 39-13-108, and the page says no deed can issue after six years from the original sale.

The page gives conflicting timeframes for deed applications, four years in some places and five in others, so call the treasurer before relying on a date.

sections.h2: What can you do about unpaid tax before selling in Campbell County?
sections.html:
Start by asking the Treasurer for the exact balance, then decide how you want to close. Wyoming bills are due in two halves, November 10 and May 10, and the Campbell tax sale page confirms those dates for new-year taxes, with interest starting the day after each due date.

An unpaid balance does not stop you from selling, but it has to be dealt with at closing. A cash buyer can take the house as-is, and the title company can pay the county from the sale proceeds.

Offices to call:

  • Treasurer, 500 S. Gillette Ave., Suite 1700, Gillette: 307-682-7268
  • Assessor, Suite 1300 in the same building: 307-682-7266
  • County Clerk: 307-682-7285
  • Planning and Zoning, and Building, through Public Works: 307-682-1970

The Treasurer also keeps a Wright office at 395 Lariat Way, open Wednesdays from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., weather permitting.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Campbell County, Wyoming?
faqs.a: The Campbell County Treasurer bills and collects it. The Assessor's Office only values the property, and says on its page that it does not set or collect tax.

faqs.q: What percent of value is a Campbell County home taxed on?
faqs.a: 9.5 percent of fair market value. The mill levy for your location is then applied to that assessed value, and levies for homes run from 65 to 80 mills according to University of Wyoming Extension.

faqs.q: How long do I have to contest my Campbell County valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the date the assessment schedule was sent. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 sets the window, so file your written statement with the assessor early and check the county's Important Dates page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Campbell County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the balance has to be paid or handled at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure, and call us at (424) 435-2326 if you want a written cash offer for the house as it stands.

faqs.q: What happens at a Campbell County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county sells a lien, not the house. A bidder pays the delinquent taxes, interest and costs and receives a certificate of purchase, and the owner can redeem by paying what the county page lists.

faqs.q: Does Campbell County have a homeowner exemption?
faqs.a: Wyoming's 25 percent exemption on the first $1 million of value applies to owner-occupied single-family homes from tax year 2025. Owners had to file an affidavit with the assessor by March 1 in 2026, so confirm the current deadline.
